To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the joint distribution of a group-sequential parameter estimator is the same as that of a sequence of independent means, asymptotically or exactly.

(a) the joint distribution of a group-sequential test statistic has the form of the joint distribution of an increasing number (the number of analyses) of means of independent and identically distributed normal random variables, and (b) this result holds exactly for normal linear models, asymptotically for generalized linear models, and asymptotically for the Cox model for survival data.

the joint distribution of parameter estimates at each stage is approximately normal, that the variance-covariance matrix of the joint distribution is approximately the same as the variance-coviance matrix at the final analysis, and that the joint distribution has the same structure at each stage as the joint distribution of means of an independent, identically normal sequence of random variables.
